cf.title: Caching a partition index's parent OID in the relcache?

input.subject: Caching a partition index's parent OID in the relcache?

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the problem is stated, measured, and already flagged by an XXX comment in the code. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable level 2 point about where the subtree invalidation rule lives and what enforces it. A committer who knows relcache invalidation has to judge that rule, together with the unanswered locking question.

brief.title: Cache partition index ancestor list in the relcache for ON CONFLICT
brief.problem: For INSERT ... ON CONFLICT on partitioned tables, ExecInitPartitionInfo() calls get_partition_ancestors() once per leaf-partition index, and each call scans pg_inherits once per hierarchy level. The cost grows with the number of indexes per leaf and with partitioning depth, and it hits workloads doing repeated upserts. An existing XXX comment in that loop already flags it as slow.
brief.proposed_design: v2 adds get_partition_index_ancestors(), which lazily caches the full ancestor list on the index's relcache entry as a single OID or an array in CacheMemoryContext. The cache resets on full relcache rebuild and in RelationReloadIndexInfo(). Because pg_inherits changes send no relcache invalidation, IndexSetParentIndex() now invalidates the whole descendant-index subtree via find_all_inheritors().
user_visible_surface: C API: new function get_partition_index_ancestors(Relation indexRel) in catalog/partition.h.
C API: new RelationData fields rd_partancestorcount and rd_partancestors in utils/rel.h.
author_claims: v2 gives +16% to +31% TPS on a 64-leaf table with 4 to 15 indexes per leaf (pgbench, 8 clients).
With 8 indexes, patched TPS stays about flat from 1 to 4 levels, while master drops from 12179 to 8442.
In perf, get_partition_ancestors falls from about 85% of time (children) to under 2%.
ATTACH plus DETACH with 256 leaf subpartitions goes from about 10 ms to 31 ms; the author calls this acceptable because re-parenting is rare.
A cold first statement still scans pg_inherits; only repeated upserts benefit (stated for v1).
brief.thread_state: Álvaro Herrera proposed caching the full ancestor list and supported the subtree invalidation in IndexSetParentIndex(); v2 follows that. Mihail Nikalayeu linked a related thread without reviewing; the author's questions on invalidation placement and NoLock in find_all_inheritors() have no answer.
unclear: The material does not say whether NoLock in find_all_inheritors() is safe on every path that calls IndexSetParentIndex(), beyond ATTACH and DETACH.
The material does not say whether REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, which v1 relied on for invalidation, still invalidates descendant caches correctly in v2.
The linked thread from Mihail Nikalayeu is not shown, so its relation to this patch is unknown.
No benchmark covers memory use of the cached arrays with many partition indexes.
The material does not say whether other callers of get_partition_ancestors() could use the new cache.

objections.title: Cache correctness depends on one function remembering to invalidate descendants
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new path that changes an intermediate partitioned index's pg_inherits link without going through IndexSetParentIndex(). Leaf indexes keep stale ancestor lists. Users find out when upserts fail with "invalid arbiter index list" or resolve the wrong arbiter, with no assert or test failure to catch it earlier.
objections.argument: Message #3 shows that pg_inherits changes send no relcache invalidation. So v2's correctness rests on a new rule: whoever re-parents an index must invalidate the whole descendant subtree, and that rule lives only inside IndexSetParentIndex(). The proposal does not say how a future writer of pg_inherits for indexes would learn this rule, or what would fail if they missed it. The single regression test covers only the ATTACH/DETACH path, and the question in message #5 about other paths has no answer.
objections.author_must_show: Which code paths can change a partitioned index's pg_inherits link today, and what would make a future path that skips the subtree invalidation fail loudly?

critic.reasoning: Álvaro Herrera supported subtree invalidation in IndexSetParentIndex(), but the thread does not list the other paths that write pg_inherits for indexes. The v1 commit message names index_concurrently_swap() as one such path, and the question in message #5 has no answer.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: No catalog schema change, but the cache depends on pg_inherits rows, whose changes send no relcache invalidation.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: Adds rd_partancestorcount and rd_partancestors to RelationData and get_partition_index_ancestors() to catalog/partition.h.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every future path that re-parents a partitioned index must invalidate the descendant-index subtree, and only IndexSetParentIndex() does so.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Changes the arbiter-mapping loop in ExecInitPartitionInfo(); ATTACH plus DETACH with 256 leaf subpartitions slows from about 10 ms to 31 ms.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which code paths can change a partitioned index's pg_inherits link today, and what would make a future path that skips the subtree invalidation fail loudly?
Is NoLock in find_all_inheritors() safe on every path that calls IndexSetParentIndex(), including paths other than ATTACH and DETACH?
Does REINDEX CONCURRENTLY, which moves the pg_inherits link in index_concurrently_swap(), still invalidate the cached ancestor lists of descendant indexes in v2?
How much memory do the cached ancestor arrays use in a backend that opens many partition indexes in a hierarchy of three or more levels?
Can other callers of get_partition_ancestors() use the new cache, or does get_partition_index_ancestors() serve only the arbiter loop?

committability.owner_note: Álvaro Herrera proposed the full-list design in message #2 and, per the brief, supported the subtree invalidation. The owner must know relcache invalidation and partitioned-index DDL.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the rule that every index re-parent invalidates the descendant-index subtree. A missed path gives a wrong arbiter or "invalid arbiter index list" errors, for as long as the cache exists.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after the review in message #2, measured the ATTACH and DETACH cost, and moved the entry to the next CommitFest on 2026-10-01.

priority.reason: The patch gives 16% to 31% more TPS for repeated upserts on partitioned tables with several indexes per leaf, and a committer shaped the design. The patch is small (about 17 KB) but changes relcache invalidation, and the code was not read here.

provisional_note: Without the code, this review could not check whether the cache is reset on every relcache path, whether the NoLock subtree scan is safe, or whether index_concurrently_swap() invalidates descendants. Only 3 of 7 thread messages were shown.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Separate memory contexts for relcache and catcache
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves catcache and relcache entries out of CacheMemoryContext into their own child contexts, CatCacheMemoryContext and RelCacheMemoryContext, so that pg_backend_memory_contexts shows each cache's memory use. Later versions added more child contexts, such as PlanCacheContext, SPICacheContext and TypCacheContext, and a separate patch changed the initial context sizes.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund's messages are not shown, but Jeff Davis reports Andres's concern that the extra contexts add memory fragmentation in each backend. Jeff saw rough consensus only for CatCacheContext and RelCacheContext, and the thread was still looking for ways to reduce the fragmentation. Rahila Syed and Ashutosh Bapat found little value in PlanCacheContext and SPICacheContext, which hold no allocations of their own. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback, citing the open feedback and concerns.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Andres's concern, IIUC, is that the additional memory contexts will cause additional fragmentation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert my ill-considered change that made formrdesc not insert the correct relation rowtype OID into the relcache entries it builds.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert my ill-considered change that made formrdesc not insert the correct relation rowtype OID into the relcache entries it builds.  This ensures that catcache copies of the relation tupdescs will be fully correct. While the deficiency doesn't seem to have any effect in the current sources, we have been bitten by not-quite-right catcache tupdescs before, so it seems like a good idea to maintain the rule that they should be right.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow logical replication via inheritance root table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets an extension or user mark an existing inheritance child so that logical replication publishes its changes through a chosen parent, reusing the publish_via_partition_root machinery. It adds a publisher-side function that tells the subscriber which tables to COPY during initial sync, and later a publish_via_parent reloption set with ALTER TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author paused the entry after finding that the subscriber side could not handle the routed data: when incoming tuples are moved to other tables, a later UPDATE or DELETE checks the root table and does not find the rows. He decided to work on subscriber-side support first. Amit Kapila also said that one extension's needs are not a reason to accept the feature in core.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Given that, I think I need to pivot and focus on the subscriber side first. That might(?) be a smaller effort anyway, and if we can't make headway there then publisher-side support probably doesn't make sense at all.

precedents_retrieved.title: table inheritance versus column compression and storage settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change how MergeAttributes() handles column compression and storage settings under table inheritance, treating them as physical per-table properties. A new child inherits the parent's settings but can override them, attaching a child changes nothing, and conflicting settings from multiple parents require an explicit setting in the child.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The committed patch was reverted after Tom Lane showed that pg_dump and pg_restore of the regression database fail: stchild4 does not restore and stchild5 gets the wrong attstorage. Ashutosh Bapat then found related existing dump bugs and proposed setting defaults when parents conflict. Peter Eisentraut declined to take on that change late in the cycle, citing unexpected pitfalls, missing test coverage and no patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
We have already discovered with the previous attempt that
there are unexpected pitfalls and lacking test coverage.  Also, there
isn't even a patch yet.

precedents_retrieved.title: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned index
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY support for partitioned indexes. It changes index_drop() to expand a partitioned index into the list of its partition indexes and run the concurrent drop steps on all of them in two transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier disliked the new code path for deleting dependent objects in the partition tree and said the problem needed more design work first. The patch then stopped applying to HEAD, and the author withdrew it until the related patch for CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on partitioned tables makes progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looking
quicky at the patch, I am not much a fan of the new code path
introduced for the deletion of dependent objects in the partition
tree, so my gut is telling me that we need to think harder about the
problem at hand first.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Don't lock partitions pruned by initial pruning"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Don't lock partitions pruned by initial pruning"
Reverted commit(s): Ensure first ModifyTable rel initialized if all are pruned
precedents_retrieved.objection:
As pointed out by Tom Lane, the patch introduced fragile and invasive
design around plan invalidation handling when locking of prunable
partitions was deferred from plancache.c to the executor. In
particular, it violated assumptions about CachedPlan immutability and
altered executor APIs in ways that are difficult to justify given the
added complexity and overhead.

This also removes the firstResultRels field added to PlannedStmt in
commit 28317de72, which was intended to support deferred locking of
certain ModifyTable result relations.

precedents_retrieved.title: refactor ExecInitPartitionInfo
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andreas Karlsson, Haibo Yan, Heikki Linnakangas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the repeated lazy `if (part_attmap == NULL) build_attrmap_by_name(...)` blocks in ExecInitPartitionInfo with one up-front build of the attribute map. The map is built under one combined condition on the ModifyTable node, partly to make room for ON CONFLICT DO SELECT.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andreas Karlsson said the v2 version builds the map almost unconditionally, so it does extra work. Haibo Yan said the v3 version gains neither performance nor readability, because the current lazy code keeps each build next to its use. A central condition is also easy to miss when a new path needs the map. Heikki Linnakangas agreed and marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: If a new path is added later that needs part_attmap, it is easier to miss updating the centralized condition than it is to keep the existing lazy initialization near the place where it is used.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use variadic macros for syscache lookup functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the numbered syscache lookup functions such as SearchSysCache1() with one variadic macro, SearchSysCache(), that counts its key arguments. It follows an earlier, already committed change that rewrote the syscache.c table with designated initializers and a KEY() macro.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that removing the numbered variants would make it hard for extensions to support several Postgres major versions, since they would have to copy the syscache.h changes. The author agreed the small gain in core readability was not worth keeping compatibility macros and withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm worried that if we are removing the variants with the explicit
numbers, it will make it difficult for extensions to maintain
compatibility with previous PG major versions.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve the performance of nested loop join in the case of partitioned inner table
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes a nested loop join skip partition pruning for a partitioned inner table when the nested loop parameters did not change since the previous outer row. The check lives in nodeNestloop.c.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author's own benchmark showed about a 4% slowdown when the parameter changes on every outer row, against about 20% gain when it stays the same. David Rowley judged that changed parameters are the common case and asked for a planner decision based on n_distinct or an executor heuristic, with the logic moved out of nodeNestloop.c. The author did not post an update, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In short, I think you're going to have to come up with something very
crafty here to reduce the overhead worst case.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix severe performance regression with gettext 0.20+ on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows with gettext 0.20 and later, the patch sets LC_MESSAGES in Windows locale format ("English_United States.1252") instead of converting it with IsoLocaleName(). This avoids a gettext bug where failed locale lookups were not cached, so every gettext() call enumerated all system locales and exception-heavy workloads ran about 5 times slower.
precedents_retrieved.objection: gettext 1.0 fixed the upstream caching bug, which made the workaround unnecessary. Peter Eisentraut found gettext 1.0 alone about 10 times faster, and the patch on top of it about 25% slower. The author traced this to an uncached Windows-format path in gettext and concluded the patch is not needed for gettext 1.0 and later.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
But when I apply your patch, it actually makes things worse (by about
25%).

To allow inserts in parallel-mode this feature has to ensure that all the
constraints, triggers, etc. are parallel-safe for the partition hierarchy

domains, etc. to determine the parallel-safety.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table."
Reverted commit(s): Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 8355a011a0124bdf7ccbada206a967d427039553, which
turns out to have been a misguided effort.  We can't really support
this in a partitioning hierarchy after all for exactly the reasons
stated in the documentation removed by that commit.  It's still
possible to use ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING (or for that matter ON
CONFLICT .. DO UPDATE) on individual partitions if desired, but
but to allow this on a partitioned table implies that we have some
way of evaluating uniqueness across the whole partitioning
hierarchy, which is false.

Shinoda Noriyoshi noticed that the old code was crashing (which we
could fix, though not in a nice way) and Amit Langote realized
that this was indicative of a fundamental problem with the commit
being reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at the same or a similar idea. Message #2 points to an earlier commit that added the arbiter-mapping code without measuring its cost, and message #6 links a related thread whose content is not shown, so no earlier rejection reason can be checked or applied.

The patch adds no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog object, dump state or psql change, and query results stay the same. Its only visible effects are the slower ATTACH/DETACH on deep hierarchies and the new RelationData fields, which belong to the performance and extension API angles. It targets master only, so backpatching does not apply.

The patch adds only backend-local relcache fields plus extra relcache invalidations from IndexSetParentIndex(). Those invalidations travel in the commit record as usual, so hot standby backends receive them. There is no on-disk, WAL-format, catalog, pg_upgrade or wire change, and the RelationData change targets master only. Whether the invalidation is correct on every re-parent path (such as DETACH CONCURRENTLY) is a design question for another angle.

The proposal adds an internal relcache cache and extra invalidations, with no new privilege check, SQL surface or exposed data. The added invalidation cost lands only on ATTACH and DETACH, which need table ownership, and the cached arrays grow with the number of index relcache entries a backend opens. A stale cache would be a correctness problem, which other angles cover.

Other maintenance points look settled. A committer who knows the area (message #2, message #4) proposed the design. Non-users gain on the hot path, and the ATTACH/DETACH cost was measured and accepted in the thread.

No existing feature, contrib module or extension caches a partition index's ancestor list; the arbiter loop in ExecInitPartitionInfo() is executor-internal and cannot be served from outside core, and the XXX comment confirms nothing does it today. The patch extends the existing relcache and get_partition_ancestors() path, so it adds no second mechanism. Whether other callers of get_partition_ancestors() should share the cache is a design question for another angle.

No demand objection. The patch speeds up an existing, widely used path (`insert ... on conflict` on partitioned tables) that an XXX comment already marks as slow, and Álvaro Herrera asked for the full-list design in message #4. The extra cost falls on index re-parenting during attach and detach, which hits the same partitioned-table users who gain. The material has no field reports, but this is a fix to a common path, not a new feature that needs users.
